prim_threatened_aggregate: The column prim_threatened_aggregate records the total count of primary (e.g. residential or other main) structures threatened by each wildfire incident. | comm_threatened_aggregate: The column comm_threatened_aggregate gives the total number of commercial structures threatened by the wildfire incident. | outb_threatened_aggregate: The `outb_threatened_aggregate` column gives the total number of outbuildings (e.g. barns, sheds, garages) reported as threatened by each wildfire incident. | station_verified_in_psa: An indicator (e.g. 1/0) denoting whether the weather station used for that fire’s weather metrics was confirmed to lie within the incident’s Primary Sampling/Study Area (PSA). | dominant_strategy_25_s:  | dominant_strategy_50_s:  | dominant_strategy_75_s: The column dominant_strategy_75_s is a categorical code for the wildfire suppression strategy that predominated around the 75th‐percentile point of the incident’s progression. | injuries_to_date_last: The injuries_to_date_last column gives the total number of reported human injuries for each wildfire incident as of the last recorded update. | control_day_of_year: The control_day_of_year column gives the ordinal day (1–365/366) of the year on which each fire was declared controlled. | start_day_of_year: The start_day_of_year field is the ordinal day (1–365/366) within the year on which each wildfire incident began. | total_fire_region: A count of all wildfire incidents recorded in the same region (as given by region/region_ind) over the same year as that fire. | dom_strat_ind_75: A numeric code identifying the dominant firefighting (suppression) strategy at the 75th-percentile level for each wildfire incident. | dom_strat_ind_25: An integer code for the “dominant strategy” label given in dominant_strategy_25_s – i.e. the categorical index (indicator) of the wildfire‐suppression strategy identified at the 25th‐percentile station for that incident. | hec:  | cause: The cause column is a categorical label indicating each wildfire’s ignition source (e.g. lightning, campfire, equipment, arson, etc.). | state: The U.S. state in which each wildfire incident occurred. | gt_100: A likely binary flag (0/1) indicating whether the fire’s Energy Release Component (ERC) exceeded 100 during the incident. | region: The `region` column is simply the named geographic area or management region (e.g. a U.S. Forest Service or Interagency fire‐management region) in which each wildfire incident occurred. | dom_strat_ind_50: A numeric code for the dominant fire‐suppression strategy used during the middle (50th percentile) segment of each wildfire incident. | erc_med: The column erc_med is the median Energy Release Component (ERC) value for the incident period—a fire-weather index measuring the potential heat (energy) release. | latitude: The latitude column gives the geographic (decimal‐degree) north–south coordinate of each wildfire incident’s location. | duration: The duration column gives the length of each wildfire incident (i.e. the number of days from its start_date to its controlled_date). | rain_sum: rain_sum: Total accumulated rainfall (precipitation) recorded over the wildfire incident period. | wind_med: The wind_med column gives the median wind‐speed (e.g. from the on‐site weather station) over the fire’s observation period. | cause_ind: A numeric encoding of the fire’s reported cause (i.e. a coded version of the “cause” field). | longitude: The longitude column gives the east–west geographic coordinate (in decimal degrees) of each wildfire incident’s location. | avrh_mean: avrh_mean: the mean (average) relative humidity recorded over the fire incident period. | start_date: The calendar date on which each wildfire incident began. | region_ind: A numeric code giving the geographic region in which each fire incident occurred (i.e. a region “index” matching the text region field). | start_year: The calendar year in which each wildfire incident began. | control_year: The calendar year in which each wildfire was brought under control (i.e. the year extracted from its controlled_date). | incident_name: The `incident_name` column gives the official name assigned to each wildfire incident in the Fire_Weather_Data_2002-2014_2016 dataset. | total_fire_west: total_fire_west  
  The total number of wildfire incidents recorded in the U.S. “West” region for the same time frame (e.g. the same year) as each listed fire. | fatalities_last: The “fatalities_last” column gives the total number of deaths attributed to that wildfire incident as of its most recent recorded update. | controlled_date: The date on which each wildfire incident was declared controlled (i.e., brought under containment). | incident_number: The incident_number column is the unique identifier assigned to each wildfire incident in the dataset. | subdom_strategy: The subdom_strategy column denotes the secondary (i.e. second-most-frequently used) wildfire suppression strategy applied during that fire incident.

Geographic Area: The Geographic Area column lists the specific jurisdiction (e.g. the United States total, individual states and territories) for which each set of population estimates is reported. | April 1, 2020 Estimates Base: The “April 1, 2020 Estimates Base” column is simply the official April 1, 2020 census count used as the starting population figure for producing the subsequent annual estimates. | Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2024): The “Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2024)” column gives the U.S. Census Bureau’s mid-year 2024 resident population estimate for each listed geographic area. | Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2023): The “Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2023)” column gives the U.S. Census Bureau’s estimated resident population for each listed geographic area on July 1, 2023, as part of the NST-EST2024-POP state and national estimates series. | Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2022): The “Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2022)” column gives the U.S. Census Bureau’s mid-year (July 1) 2022 population estimate for each listed geographic area. | Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2021): The “Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2021)” column gives the U.S. Census Bureau’s annual estimated resident population for each listed geographic area on July 1, 2021. | Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2020): The “Population Estimate (as of July 1, 2020)” column gives the U.S. Census Bureau’s estimate of the resident population for each listed geographic area on July 1, 2020.

y: The “y” column is the projected northing coordinate (Y) of each RAWS station in the dataset’s map projection. | x: The “x” column is the projected (easting) coordinate of each RAWS station location in the dataset’s map projection. | Unit: The “Unit” field identifies the administrative land unit (e.g. National Forest, grassland, park, agency subdivision) responsible for or hosting that RAWS station. | State: The U.S. state (typically as a two-letter postal abbreviation) in which the weather station is located. | WX ID: The “WX ID” column is the station’s unique weather‐station identifier code. | Status: The Status column flags each RAWS station’s current operational state (e.g. active, inactive/offline, under maintenance). | Region: The “Region” field indicates the USDA Forest Service administrative region (e.g. Region 1–10) in which each RAWS (Remote Automated Weather Station) is located. | Agency: The “Agency” column identifies the government or managing organization responsible for each RAWS (Remote Automated Weather Station). | County: The County column indicates the U.S. county in which each RAWS (Remote Automated Weather Station) observation site is located. | NWS ID: The NWS ID column holds the station’s unique identifier as assigned by the U.S. National Weather Service. | NESS ID: No description. | Ob Time: The “Ob Time” column is the timestamp of each RAWS station observation—that is, the date and time when that weather reading was taken. | Sub-Unit: No description. | Latitude: The Latitude column gives each RAWS weather station’s geographic north–south coordinate in decimal degrees. | OBJECTID: The OBJECTID column is simply the internal, unique integer key assigned to each record (row) in the PublicView_RAWS dataset. | Longitude: The “Longitude” column gives the east–west geographic coordinate (in decimal degrees) of each RAWS wildfire monitoring station. | Elevation: The station’s elevation above mean sea level. | Station ID: The “Station ID” column is simply the unique identifier assigned to each Remote Automated Weather Station (RAWS) in this public‐view dataset. | Station Name: The Station Name column gives the human‐readable name assigned to each Remote Automated Weather Station (RAWS) in this public wildfire weather dataset. | Fuel Moisture: The “Fuel Moisture” column gives the moisture content (typically as a percentage of dry weight) of wildland vegetation “fuels” measured at each RAWS site, a key input for assessing fire behavior and risk. | Wind Speed MPH: The “Wind Speed MPH” column gives the observed wind speed at the RAWS station, measured in miles per hour. | Solar Radiation: The “Solar Radiation” column is the station’s measured incoming solar irradiance (i.e. the rate of solar energy received per unit area, typically in W/m²) as recorded by the RAWS site. | Battery Voltage: The “Battery Voltage” column gives the real-time voltage (in volts) of the remote automated weather station’s onboard battery at the time of each observation. | Fuel Temperature: The “Fuel Temperature” column gives the measured temperature of the combustible vegetation (the “fuel bed”) at the RAWS site. | Site Description: The Site Description field gives a short narrative of the RAWS station’s immediate physical setting (terrain, vegetation cover, exposure, etc.). | Relative Humidity: The “Relative Humidity” column gives, in percent, the amount of water vapor in the air at the time of observation relative to the maximum the air could hold at that temperature, as measured by the RAWS wildfire‐monitoring station. | Rain Accumulation: Rain Accumulation: the total precipitation (rainfall) recorded by the RAWS station over its reporting interval. | MesoWest Station ID: The “MesoWest Station ID” column gives the unique identifier that MesoWest assigns to each RAWS site for linking into its detailed weather data. | Wind Speed Peak MPH: The highest wind gust (peak wind speed) recorded, in miles per hour, by the RAWS station for that observation period. | Wind Direction, Peak: In this wildfire monitoring (RAWS) dataset, “Wind Direction, Peak” is the compass heading (in degrees) from which the highest wind gust during the observation period originated. | Wind Direction Degrees: The “Wind Direction Degrees” column records the compass direction from which the wind is blowing at the RAWS (Remote Automated Weather Station), expressed in degrees clockwise from true north. | NOAA Detailed Weather Link: A URL linking to the NOAA webpage with detailed weather observations for that RAWS station. | MesoWest Detailed Weather Link: A URL linking to the MesoWest webpage for that RAWS station’s detailed weather observations. | Air Temperaturee, Standard Placement: Air Temperaturee, Standard Placement: The ambient air temperature measured by the station’s standard‐height sensor (typically 1.5–2 m above ground).

the state of Iowa. | Utah: The “Utah” column gives the monthly Zillow Home Value Index (ZHVI) for residential properties in Utah. | Idaho: The “Idaho” column gives the monthly Zillow Home Value Index
